decision.source_review:
I audited the current offline material and policy proposal, not a Provider opinion or a model result. I read the four complete reports a, b, c and d; all unique request content, including baseline and candidate policies, report messages, full source projections, deterministic source and external snapshots, knowledge, complete facts/provenance pack, generation data and computed cohorts; and the unchanged review/repair schema. I verified the material SHA256. Every request report matches its named full report apart from block markers and blank-line formatting. Each baseline/candidate pair differs only in its system policy. Across cases the source facts, knowledge, user utterance, tables, external snapshots and tools are identical; the source-message differences are only source/catalog digest fields. The fact and provenance table rows agree with the complete pack. No expected labels, primary notes, retained public review or external evaluation were read. The task binding identifies offline collections and a proposal, not a new Provider receipt.

The governing user request is to observe DK ShowMaker#KR1, a person distinct from the reader, with exercises limited to observation and no conversion of these matches into the reader personal baseline or training prescription. The completion policy additionally requires substantive body use of a supported K citation and at least one matching OP.GG tier/rank/rate connected to a conditional suggestion or testable action, together with position, retrieval time and current-snapshot limits. These are existing supplied obligations, not invented preferences for more advice or different prose. All four reports provide the sample overview, comparisons, highlights, risk observations, replay checks and source boundaries. They use K2/K3 substantively to frame development/resource/participation checks as hypotheses, so none lacks the required knowledge use. The following are my independent completion-duty findings, under both policies.

Report a has one necessary completion gap at block 18: it lists OP.GG mid figures with time and limits after calling them an investigable champion-pool question, but supplies no actual question or concrete action using a particular tier/rank/rate. Other replay recommendations do not connect to those external facts. A supported conditional observation action needs to be added. There is no separately established personal-training conflict in blocks 18 or 21-22: block 2 excludes personal baseline/training use, block 20 directly scopes the options as observation exercises, and recording metrics for subsequent games, reviewing development interruptions and obtaining more samples do not say that the reader must participate in those games. The wording about practicing a role can be clarified without changing the actual observation actions; it cannot alone establish a different participant.

Report b closes that block 18 consumption gap by explicitly using Syndra Tier 2 and rank 12 as a conditional current-snapshot replay-selection clue and naming resource acquisition and participation timing as the observation checks. Syndra is a sampled MIDDLE champion with a winning match, and the supplied mid snapshot has precisely those tier/rank values. Position, retrieval time and boundaries remain in the paragraph, and the added action does not claim that the snapshot explains the historical win or predicts reader performance. It is a concrete use, rather than another disclaimer. With the same observation scope and actions as a otherwise, I find no necessary completion-duty gap in b. This is not factual clearance of b or acceptance for publication.

Report c has the same adequate OP.GG-to-action connection as b, so no OP.GG-use omission remains. It has a genuine independent task/identity conflict at block 21: the added sentence explicitly requires the reader personally to participate in the next mid games and arrange personal training from the observed player matches. This contradicts the observation-only user task and cannot be erased by the earlier scope statements or the valid block 18 action. The necessary correction is to remove that explicit personal-participation/personal-training instruction and retain the supported observation references and observation actions.

Report d has both independent gaps: the original block 18 still lacks the required external-metric-to-action connection, while the added block 21 sentence explicitly prescribes reader participation and personal training. Repairing only one would leave the other. Neither a scope disclaimer nor a valid knowledge citation excuses the explicit conflicting action. Conversely, adding an external observation action cannot retroactively justify the personal prescription.

The controls are semantically useful and preserve correct content: b adds only the external-action sentence, d adds only the explicit personal-action sentence, and c adds both. Removing those designated additions recovers a exactly. No correct source numbers, conditions or observations were deleted to construct the contrast. In particular, winning CS/min values 8.66 and 8.95 support the approximate 8.7-9.0 observation reference, and early deaths 2 and 3 support at most 3. Those values are observations, not mandatory reader performance targets. Neither adding the missing OP.GG action in a/d nor removing the explicit personal command in c/d requires deleting these correct references, rewriting the full plan, assigning a main position or asking for a reader baseline.

The candidate policy is fair enough for this bounded diagnostic. It preserves the original completion duties, facts/completion separation, source requirements, output schema and necessary-patch contract. Its added method requires reading directly governing context, distinguishes a missing participant from an explicitly conflicting participant, requires checking the whole report before declaring an action absent, and expressly says that merely listing figures or saying they can be researched does not meet the external-use duty. It also expressly prevents disclaimers from excusing a concrete conflict and requires preservation of unrelated supported facts, conditions and observation references. The exhibition analogy illustrates these already applicable distinctions without asserting RiftCoach evidence or case labels. I find no new user requirement, blanket exemption of true conflicts, or direction to remove valid observations in the proposal.

Acceptance is limited to the fairness and discriminating value of these materials for a bounded diagnostic. This is a small, closely related synthetic contrast based on one source report, with deliberately explicit positive controls and an illustrative policy example close to the tested distinction. It does not establish performance on subtler identity drift, different wording or independent reports; a successful later contrast would not by itself establish general improvement. There are no Provider outputs, actual applications or fresh evidence here, so candidate efficacy and model improvement remain unproven. Shared original factual matters, including the Vex ban-rate label and the Anivia winner grouping, remain for facts-duty review; the candidate does not waive them. No report/model acceptance, reopening of a closed batch, business validation or publication follows from this material acceptance.
